newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India rises as value buyers emerge.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India rises as value buyers emerge.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) rose sharply in active trade as investors perceived better value in the GDRs and local market.
"This market has not turned the corner but there has generally been very good business with the local market around 3,000 points," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed up 1.10 points, 1.83 percent, at 61.51 points, with the premium over the local market at 14.32 percent compared with yesterday's 13.01 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 22.50 to 3,066.66.
The BSE is closed on Friday and next Monday and Tuesday for the Hindu New Year. It will open briefly for a session on Sunday.
Traders said there had been good two-way business in Ashok Leyland, BSES, Bajaj, Hindalco and Reliance.
"We have turned over 600,000 Hindalco in the past two days," said a trader.
Buyers have also emerged for ITC, which is embroiled in a dispute over foreign exchange transfers.
"The GDR market is very sentiment-driven. I blows hot and cold and there is now a level at which people think there is value," said a trader.
The Capel Korea GDR Index fell 0.89 points, or 1.36 percent, at 63.14, a premium of 26.80 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 5.53 points to a provisional 741.76.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index lost 0.60 points, 0.66 percent, at 90.42, a premium of 0.80 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index lost 23.97 points or 0.36 percent to 6,629.68.
